answer_1.quote: We performed aesthetic fine-tuning on the open-source LLaMA series models ... and compared the aesthetic scores of the fine-tuned LLMs with state-of-the-art LLMs ... We also employed three well‑established auto‑evaluation instruction‑following benchmarks ... AlpacaEval 2.0, Arena‑Hard and MT‑Bench.

answer_2.quote: We report the win rate (WR) in text aesthetics at both the text and image levels ... We aggregated all pairwise comparisons with the baseline model to derive win rates and used bootstrapping to calculate a confidence interval, resulting in an ordered ranking of all models.

answer_3.quote: We employ the "LLM‑as‑a‑judge" framework ... using GPT-4o to evaluate text aesthetics ... we implemented a pairwise comparison method ... judges assessed aesthetic preferences on a Likert scale ... we rendered the LLM‑generated texts as HTML ... and then had GPT-4o evaluate these images.

answer_4.quote: To ensure objective and reliable results, we employed human experts for professional evaluation. ... We randomly sample fifty entries ... ask human annotators to rate the aesthetics of these entries. ... The annotators were introduced to the four evaluation dimensions—clarity, layout, uniformity, and coherence—and practiced with a subset of the dataset.
answer_4.guideline: Human annotators rated the generated texts on four dimensions: clarity, layout, uniformity, and coherence using a Likert‑style rubric.
